description: Batched MCTS values new leaves several at a time, as a neural network on a GPU wants to, instead of one per simulation. A simulation stops at its new leaf and waits; until the batch is valued, selection counts every waiting simulation as a loss for the side that chose it (*virtual loss*), so the next simulations of the batch spread over other moves instead of piling onto the same leaf. Then one evaluator call values the batch, the values are backed up, the virtual losses are removed, and the priors it returns are set on the leaves' moves. A finished game is valued at once, and on a new tree the root goes to the evaluator first, for the priors of its moves. Use it when leaf evaluation is expensive and cheaper per leaf in batches; with a batch of one it is plain MCTS.
